title: Mole Negro
subtitle: Oaxacan black mole sauce with chicken
excerpt: One of the most complex sauces in the world: Oaxacan mole negro is built from dried chillies, charred tomatoes, toasted seeds, dark chocolate, and over twenty aromatics reduced to a deep, almost-black sauce. A project worth every hour it takes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Mole negro is the most complex and celebrated of the seven traditional moles of Oaxaca, Mexico, and is considered one of the most sophisticated sauces in the world, requiring between 20 and 30 ingredients and several hours of preparation. The black colour comes from the charring of the chilli seeds and the addition of dark chocolate (Mexican cooking chocolate, which is coarser and less sweet than European chocolate). The sauce is built in stages: dried chillies are soaked and toasted, seeds and spices are dry-toasted separately, tomatoes and onion are charred, and everything is blended in stages with stock and cooked down for over an hour. Mole negro traditionally accompanies turkey (guajolote) for celebrations; chicken is the everyday version. The sauce freezes well and a large batch will provide multiple meals.

content.text: The chillies should be wiped rather than washed; moisture prevents them toasting properly. Toast each component separately as they all require different times. The sauce must be cooked long enough after blending for the raw chilli flavour to cook out, usually at least 45 minutes of simmering. Mulato and ancho chillies are available from Mexican food importers and online; pasilla is widely stocked.

Toast the dried chillies in a dry pan for 30 seconds per side until fragrant. Soak in hot water for 20 minutes. Drain and set aside. Separately toast the sesame and pumpkin seeds in the dry pan until golden.
Blend the soaked chillies with the charred onion, garlic, tinned tomatoes, seeds, raisins, spices, and 200 ml of stock until very smooth. Pass through a sieve if you want a very smooth sauce.

Fry the sauce in the hot oil in a wide pan, stirring constantly, for 10 minutes until it darkens. Add the remaining stock and chocolate. Simmer for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally. Brown the chicken thighs and cook them in the mole for 30 minutes until cooked through. Serve with white rice and warm tortillas.
